lane.objective: Infer basement relief from the supplied isostatic gravity; use USGS GP-1012 only to calibrate regional depth scale; identify basement-depth horizontal-gradient steps; emit multi-line ribbons; compare withheld basin-interior segment recovery with equal-budget random lines.
lane.named_non_fault_mimic: Intrabasement lithologic/density contrasts can create a gravity step without a fault. Terrain mimics include alluvial-fan toes, terrace risers, channels, landslides, roads, and mines.

top_candidate.hypothesis: Use 3DEP-derived terrain scarp descriptors to build three-cell ribbons inside the inverted basement-step corridor and basin fill.
top_candidate.layers: Public 12-band terrain-descriptor raster derived upstream from USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM work; provisional basement-depth HGM steps and basin mask; no catalogue features in surface generation.
top_candidate.physical_signature: Metre-scale slope breaks with paired crest/base curvature and coherent strike, spatially associated with a basement-depth step.
top_candidate.catalogue_gap_rationale: Low scarps in Quaternary fans may be below regional mapping scale; high-resolution terrain descriptors could expose concealed young splays, while the gravity corridor constrains them to a buried step.
top_candidate.difference_from_implemented_work: The archived H61-G construction used in-corridor elevation-slope dots, not lidar-derived ribbons. The merged main branch also contains H61-MH, an inversion-feature out-of-fold habitat model whose final TIFF fails the strict final-dot gate. This H61-L screen is a distinct terrain-plus-gravity-surface hypothesis, and sibling terrain rasters are not used as predictions.
top_candidate.expected_dti_gain: Highest qualitative prior among the five candidates; PROJECTION ONLY, not measured. The candidate failed the pre-placement uniqueness gate, so gain was not holdout-tested.
top_candidate.implementation_cost: High data volume; one surface screen; no H61-L holdout or weekly slot.

ranked_hypotheses.name: 1 m lidar scarp detection restricted to gravity corridors
ranked_hypotheses.layers: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM (organiser's 1m_DEM_links.csv; public domain) → scarp-likelihood raster; this session's ±1 km basement-step corridor and basin mask as prior.
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: Metre-scale topographic steps (scarp height 0.5–5 m, slope break, curvature couplet) — the primary evidence the test-set mappers used.
ranked_hypotheses.catalogue_gap_rationale: The 1:24k–1:250k catalogue missed low scarps in Quaternary fans; 1 m data resolves them; the corridor removes fan-toe/terrace mimics that have no basement step.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_implemented_work: Unlike archived H61-G, which used band-19 slope-ridge dots, this tests 3DEP-derived scarp morphology as multi-line ribbons inside an inverted basement-step corridor. The merged main branch also tested H61-MH, a gravity/inversion-feature out-of-fold habitat model; it did not test this 3DEP scarp-ribbon surface. The terrain raster is a public sibling derivative, not raw DEM/lidar tiles.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Highest expected value by expert prior (PROJECTION, not a score); PRE-PLACEMENT UNIQUENESS STOP: 94.6692% of positive scarp-ribbon surface pixels are within 3 px of the prior near-blanket raster, above the literal 70% threshold. HOLDOUT NOT RUN.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: High data volume; public sibling-derived 12-band descriptor file already fetched and SHA-256 verified. One candidate surface built; no holdout or submission slot used.
ranked_hypotheses.holdout_status: NOT RUN — strict surface gate stop

ranked_hypotheses.name: Piedmont belt: basinward of the inverted bedrock–fill contact
ranked_hypotheses.layers: Inverted depth = 0 contour (bedrock outcrop boundary) buffered 0–2 km basinward; band 12 detrended elevation curvature; band 19 slope ridges.
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: Range-front normal faults step basinward through time; young splays and antithetic strands sit 0–2 km in front of the mapped range-front trace as low scarps across fans.
ranked_hypotheses.catalogue_gap_rationale: The catalogue holds the main range-front trace; piedmont splays are the commonest unmapped class in Basin-and-Range compilations.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_implemented_work: H61-MH included a basin indicator and step/corridor features in a learned model, but did not isolate an explicit 0–2 km basinward piedmont belt as its own spatial hypothesis or emit ribbons there.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Moderate. The screen's highest prior-only enrichment (1.7× random for pixels inside the gravity corridor, all depths) sits at the range fronts. PROJECTION.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low (all inputs cached). One holdout run.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Gravity-step × magnetic-edge conjunction (intrabasin faults offsetting magnetic basement or flows)
ranked_hypotheses.layers: Corridor from the inversion; band 3 TMI horizontal-gradient maxima; band 6 tilt zero-crossings; band 9 vertical gradient.
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: A normal fault that offsets magnetised basement or volcanic flows gives a sharp magnetic edge co-located with the gravity step; GeoDAWN line spacing resolves such edges to ~300 m, unlike regional gravity.
ranked_hypotheses.catalogue_gap_rationale: Concealed under alluvium; surface mapping cannot see them. Co-location rejects intrabasement density contacts that have no magnetic expression (the lane's named mimic).
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_implemented_work: H61-MH used the 19 supplied bands in a learned habitat model, but did not implement this explicit gravity-step × magnetic-edge conjunction as a test of the intrabasement-contact mimic; H61-C only proposed magnetic fabric as an oracle.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Low–moderate: precision ×1.5 plausible, recall small (few magnetic basins). PROJECTION.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Source-depth consistency filter (Euler SI = 0) to reject intrabasement contacts
ranked_hypotheses.layers: Band 13 gravity, band 5 horizontal gradient, band 11 vertical gradient → contact-depth estimate; compare with inverted basin depth.
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: A basement step has source depth ≈ fill thickness; an intrabasement density contrast has source depth ≫ fill thickness.
ranked_hypotheses.catalogue_gap_rationale: Directly tests the lane's competing explanation; improves the purity of X1-type candidates.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_implemented_work: H61-MH included Euler SI=0 source depth as a weak model feature, but did not implement a hard source-depth-versus-inverted-fill-thickness consistency filter; this decision rule remains untested.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Low: raises precision of a candidate family whose recall is already tiny (X1a 0.023). PROJECTION.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Scale-persistent paired-flank basement-step ribbons with magnetic corroboration
ranked_hypotheses.layers: Supplied isostatic gravity → provisional inverted basement depth and its horizontal gradients at 200/400/800 m; supplied TMI/tilt/vertical-gradient magnetic bands as corroboration only. GP-1012 calibrates the regional depth scale.
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: A candidate step has paired cross-profile gradient flanks of opposite sign, coherent strike, and a persistent location across scales; a co-located magnetic edge supports but is not required for the ribbon.
ranked_hypotheses.catalogue_gap_rationale: Buried basin-interior faults can be omitted or fragmented in the mapped catalogue. Pairing, strike continuity, and scale persistence may suppress isolated density contacts/noise while allowing multi-line fault ribbons under alluvium; magnetics provide an independent but imperfect corroborating signature.
ranked_hypotheses.difference_from_implemented_work: Distinct from H61-MH, which used supplied bands and inversion-derived variables in a learned habitat model, and from H61-H, which proposed simple gravity/magnetic edge conjunction. This untested rule matches paired flank geometry and scale persistence before ribbon emission; it uses no catalogue-derived candidate features.
ranked_hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Low-to-moderate expected gain, PROJECTION ONLY: paired-flank geometry may improve precision, while requiring magnetic corroboration can lose faults without magnetised offsets. No measured DTI.
ranked_hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high: compute multi-scale derivatives, orientation-aware cross-profile pairs, and pre-placement registry gates; run one holdout only if the surface first clears.
